metadata.description: Chroma or VecturaDB on one Azure VM with Docker, the data on a managed disk.
Name of the VM, and prefix of the other resources: 2 to 20 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
Region of the resources.
The server: chroma (Chroma 1.5.9) or vecturadb (VecturaDB, built from Chroma, with sparse vectors, BM25, the Search API, collection fork and API keys).
Image of Chroma. The same image is on Docker Hub as chromadb/chroma.
Image of VecturaDB.
Size of the VM. Tested: Standard_B2pts_v2 (Arm), Standard_B1s, Standard_B1ms. Standard_B1ls runs out of memory at the first boot.
CPU of the VM size. auto: arm64 when the letters after the size number hold a p, like Standard_B2pts_v2 or Standard_D2ps_v5, x64 otherwise.

Who reaches the server: internal (only the virtual network, HTTP on the private address), allowed-ips (HTTPS from the allowed IP ranges), or public (HTTPS from anywhere, VecturaDB with an API key only).
IP ranges, in CIDR notation, that may reach the server over HTTPS when access is allowed-ips.
VecturaDB only: the API key of the admin user. Every request then needs it, in the x-chroma-token header. Required when access is public.
Your own domain name for HTTPS, like chroma.example.com, with a DNS A record to the public IP. Empty: the Azure name of the public IP.
Email for the account of the HTTPS certificate at Let's Encrypt. Optional.
Size of the data disk in GiB (Standard SSD).
Name of the admin account of the VM.
SSH public key of the admin account. Port 22 stays closed: the key is only for access through Azure Bastion or after you open the port yourself.
Backups of the data disk: disk (Azure Disk Backup, incremental snapshots) or none.
Hours between two backups of the data disk.
Days a backup is kept.
Soft delete of the backup vault. On keeps deleted backups for 14 days, against a deletion by mistake or by an attacker; the vault then stays 14 days after its deletion. Off only for tests.
Time of the deployment: leave the default. A run command with unchanged properties does not run again, so this value makes every deployment run configure.sh, even with the same parameters.

variables.$fxv#0:
#!/bin/bash
# First boot of the VM: the data disk, Docker and Caddy. The server itself is set up by configure.sh, which the
# template runs at every deployment.
set -eux
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# The data disk at LUN 0: formatted once, mounted at /var/lib/chroma.
disk=""
for i in $(seq 1 90); do
  for d in /dev/disk/azure/data/by-lun/0 /dev/disk/azure/scsi1/lun0; do
    if [ -e "$d" ]; then disk=$d; break 2; fi
  done
  sleep 2
done
[ -n "$disk" ] || { echo "no data disk at LUN 0"; exit 1; }
blkid "$disk" >/dev/null 2>&1 || mkfs.ext4 -q -L chroma-data "$disk"
mkdir -p /var/lib/chroma
grep -q 'LABEL=chroma-data' /etc/fstab || echo 'LABEL=chroma-data /var/lib/chroma ext4 defaults,nofail,discard 0 2' >> /etc/fstab
mount -a
mountpoint -q /var/lib/chroma

# Docker, with bounded logs.
mkdir -p /etc/docker
cat > /etc/docker/daemon.json <<'EOF'
{"log-driver": "json-file", "log-opts": {"max-size": "10m", "max-file": "3"}}
EOF
apt-get update -q
apt-get install -y -q docker.io curl gnupg debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https
systemctl enable --now docker

# Caddy from its official apt repository, which is signed. Ubuntu 24.04 has an older Caddy in universe.
curl -1sLf https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
apt-get update -q
apt-get install -y -q caddy
systemctl disable --now caddy

touch /var/lib/chroma-first-boot-done
variables.$fxv#1:
#!/bin/sh
# Run Command of the template, at every deployment: starts the server with the image and the settings of this
# deployment. The old container stops before the new one starts, so one process at a time works on /var/lib/chroma.
# Parameters arrive as environment variables: ENGINE, IMAGE, ACCESS (internal, allowed-ips, public), HOST,
# ALLOWED_IPS (separated by spaces), ACME_EMAIL, DEPLOYED_AT (the time of the deployment, which makes every
# deployment run this script), and API_KEY (protected). POSIX sh, whatever shell runs it.
set -eu
echo "deployment of ${DEPLOYED_AT:-unknown time}"
cloud-init status --wait >/dev/null || true
[ -e /var/lib/chroma-first-boot-done ] || { echo "the first boot did not finish: see /var/log/cloud-init-output.log"; exit 1; }
mountpoint -q /var/lib/chroma || { echo "the data disk is not mounted at /var/lib/chroma"; exit 1; }

# Docker starts only once the data disk is mounted. The fstab line has nofail, which does not hold back the services:
# a VM that boots without the disk would otherwise serve an empty database from the OS disk.
mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d
printf '[Unit]\nRequiresMountsFor=/var/lib/chroma\n' > /etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d/chroma-data.conf
systemctl daemon-reload

mkdir -p /etc/chroma
keys=no
if [ "$ENGINE" = vecturadb ] && [ -n "${API_KEY:-}" ]; then
  # The credentials file of VecturaDB, in the format of Chroma 0.5. YAML single quotes keep the key as it is.
  quoted=$(printf %s "$API_KEY" | sed "s/'/''/g")
  (umask 077; printf "users:\n  - id: admin\n    tokens:\n      - '%s'\n" "$quoted" > /etc/chroma/credentials.yaml)
  keys=yes
else
  rm -f /etc/chroma/credentials.yaml
fi

# Internal: the server answers on the private address, port 8000. Otherwise only Caddy reaches it, on 127.0.0.1.
if [ "$ACCESS" = internal ]; then publish=8000:8000; else publish=127.0.0.1:8000:8000; fi

docker pull -q "$IMAGE"
if docker inspect chroma >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  docker stop -t 30 chroma
  docker rm chroma
fi
if [ "$keys" = yes ]; then
  docker run -d --name chroma --restart unless-stopped -p "$publish" -v /var/lib/chroma:/data \
    -v /etc/chroma/credentials.yaml:/credentials/credentials.yaml:ro \
    -e CHROMA_SERVER_AUTHN_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/credentials/credentials.yaml "$IMAGE"
else
  docker run -d --name chroma --restart unless-stopped -p "$publish" -v /var/lib/chroma:/data "$IMAGE"
fi
ready=no
for i in $(seq 1 90); do
  if curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v2/heartbeat; then ready=yes; break; fi
  sleep 2
done
[ "$ready" = yes ] || { docker logs --tail 50 chroma; echo "the server did not answer"; exit 1; }

if [ "$ACCESS" = internal ]; then
  systemctl disable --now caddy || true
else
  {
    if [ -n "${ACME_EMAIL:-}" ]; then printf '{\n\temail %s\n}\n\n' "$ACME_EMAIL"; fi
    # Port 80 only answers the HTTP-01 challenge of the certificate, which Caddy handles before this block.
    printf 'http://%s {\n\tabort\n}\n\n' "$HOST"
    printf '%s {\n' "$HOST"
    if [ "$ACCESS" = allowed-ips ]; then
      printf '\t@denied not remote_ip %s\n\tabort @denied\n' "$ALLOWED_IPS"
    fi
    printf '\treverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8000\n}\n'
  } > /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
  caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile
  systemctl enable caddy
  systemctl reload-or-restart caddy
  # The deployment ends only once Caddy holds the certificate: right after the reload, HTTPS is not ready yet.
  cert=no
  for i in $(seq 1 90); do
    if ls /var/lib/caddy/.local/share/caddy/certificates/*/"$HOST"/"$HOST".crt >/dev/null 2>&1; then cert=yes; break; fi
    sleep 2
  done
  [ "$cert" = yes ] || { journalctl -u caddy --no-pager | tail -n 20; echo "no HTTPS certificate for $HOST after 180 s"; exit 1; }
fi
docker ps --filter name=chroma --format 'chroma: {{.Image}} {{.Status}}'
caddy version || true
checks: [if(and(equals(parameters('access'), 'public'), or(not(equals(parameters('engine'), 'vecturadb')), empty(parameters('apiKey')))), fail('access public needs engine vecturadb and an apiKey: Chroma 1.5.9 has no API keys.'), 'ok')]
[if(and(equals(parameters('access'), 'allowed-ips'), empty(parameters('allowedIpRanges'))), fail('access allowed-ips needs at least one range in allowedIpRanges.'), 'ok')]

properties.securityRules: [if(equals(parameters('access'), 'internal'), createArray(), createArray(createObject('name', 'certificate-challenge', 'properties', createObject('priority', 100, 'direction', 'Inbound', 'access', 'Allow', 'protocol', 'Tcp', 'sourceAddressPrefix', 'Internet', 'sourcePortRange', '*', 'destinationAddressPrefix', '*', 'destinationPortRange', '80')), createObject('name', 'https', 'properties', union(createObject('priority', 110, 'direction', 'Inbound', 'access', 'Allow', 'protocol', 'Tcp', 'sourcePortRange', '*', 'destinationAddressPrefix', '*', 'destinationPortRange', '443'), if(equals(parameters('access'), 'public'), createObject('sourceAddressPrefix', 'Internet'), createObject('sourceAddressPrefixes', parameters('allowedIpRanges')))))))]

ipConfigurations.name: ipconfig1
ipConfigurations.properties: [union(createObject('subnet', createObject('id', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks', format('{0}-vnet', parameters('name'))), '2024-05-01').subnets[0].id), 'privateIPAllocationMethod', 'Dynamic'), if(variables('isPublic'), createObject('publicIPAddress', createObject('id', resourceId('Microsoft.Network/publicIPAddresses', format('{0}-ip', parameters('name'))))), createObject()))]

metadata.description: Address for the clients.

url.value: [if(variables('isPublic'), format('https://{0}', if(empty(parameters('domainName')), reference(resourceId('Microsoft.Network/publicIPAddresses', format('{0}-ip', parameters('name'))), '2024-05-01').dnsSettings.fqdn, parameters('domainName'))), format('http://{0}:8000', reference(resourceId('Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces', format('{0}-nic', parameters('name'))), '2024-05-01').ipConfigurations[0].properties.privateIPAddress))]
